subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own hard tool-policy layer, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue relying on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This changes a public config/security boundary and decides whether cron restrictions are a new operator knob, an inherited subagent policy, or intentionally not a global policy.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Define a cron-specific hard policy layer with clear precedence against existing policies and per-job `toolsAllow`, then update schema/help/docs and regression tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron sessions as delegated runtimes for tool-policy purposes, reducing config surface but potentially surprising operators who use subagent and cron scopes differently.

options.title: Keep per-job allowlists only
options.body: Document `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery-mode safeguards as the supported approach, leaving no system-wide cron deny option.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Define a cron-specific hard policy layer with clear precedence against existing policies and per-job `toolsAllow`, then update schema/help/docs and regression tests.
